title: Algebraic Kunneth formula for tensor products of complexes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A cochain complex of $k$-vector spaces is a family of $k$-vector spaces $A^p$ ($p\in\mathbf Z$) with $k$-linear maps $d_A^p:A^p\to A^{p+1}$ and $d_A^{p+1}d_A^p=0$; it is bounded below if $A^p=0$ for all $p$ below some integer. Put $Z^p(A)=\ker(d_A^p)$, $B^p(A)=\operatorname{im}(d_A^{p-1})$ and $H^p(A)=Z^p(A)/B^p(A)$, and similarly for $B$. For two bounded-below complexes $A$ and $B$, form the total tensor-product complex with $(A\otimes_k B)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A^p\otimes_k B^q$ and differential $d_A\otimes 1+(-1)^p\,1\otimes d_B$ on $A^p\otimes_k B^q$. For every integer $n$, the map $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(A)\otimes_k H^q(B)\to H^n(A\otimes_k B)$, sending $[a]\otimes[b]$ to $[a\otimes b]$, is well defined and is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For each degree $p$ put $Z_A^p=\ker(d_A^p)$ and $B_A^p=\operatorname{im}(d_A^{p-1})$, and similarly for $B$. Since $k$ is a field, choose a complement $H_A^p$ of $B_A^p$ in $Z_A^p$ and a complement $C_A^p$ of $Z_A^p$ in $A^p$, so $A^p=B_A^p\oplus H_A^p\oplus C_A^p$. Then $d_A^p$ restricts to an isomorphism $C_A^p\xrightarrow{\sim}B_A^{p+1}$: it is injective because $C_A^p\cap\ker(d_A^p)=C_A^p\cap Z_A^p=0$, and surjective because $d_A^p(A^p)=d_A^p(C_A^p)$ and $B_A^{p+1}=\operatorname{im}(d_A^p)$. Hence $A$ is the direct sum of the subcomplexes $H_A^p[-p]$ (zero differential, as $H_A^p\subset Z_A^p$) and the two-term subcomplexes $C_A^p\to B_A^{p+1}$, and similarly for $B$; on each two-term piece, the inverse $h_A=(d_A^p|_{C_A^p})^{-1}:B_A^{p+1}\to C_A^p$, extended by $0$, satisfies $d_Ah_A+h_Ad_A=1$. (The bounded-below hypothesis is not needed for this argument, since $(A\otimes_kB)^n$ is defined as a direct sum; it is harmless.)

proof.text: Distributing the direct sums of Step 1 decomposes the total complex $A\otimes_kB$ as a direct sum of subcomplexes: $H_A\otimes_kH_B$, and tensor products in which at least one factor is a two-term piece. On a summand whose $A$-factor is a two-term piece with homotopy $h_A$ of degree $-1$, $d_Ah_A+h_Ad_A=1$, put $H(a\otimes b)=h_A(a)\otimes b$ for $a\in A^p$. In $(d_A\otimes1+(-1)^{\bullet}1\otimes d_B)H+H(d_A\otimes1+(-1)^{\bullet}1\otimes d_B)$ applied to $a\otimes b$, the mixed terms are $(-1)^{p-1}h_A(a)\otimes d_Bb$ and $(-1)^ph_A(a)\otimes d_Bb$ and cancel, leaving $(d_Ah_A+h_Ad_A)(a)\otimes b=a\otimes b$. On a summand whose $B$-factor is a two-term piece, $H(a\otimes b)=(-1)^pa\otimes h_B(b)$ for $a\in A^p$ gives, by the same calculation, $d_A a\otimes h_Bb$ terms with signs $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$ cancelling and $a\otimes(d_Bh_B+h_Bd_B)(b)=a\otimes b$ remaining. Hence every such summand is contractible, so acyclic, while $H_A\otimes_kH_B$ has zero differential.

proof.text: The map is well defined: for cocycles $a\in Z^p(A)$, $b\in Z^q(B)$ one has $d(a\otimes b)=d_Aa\otimes b+(-1)^pa\otimes d_Bb=0$, and $d(a'\otimes b)=d_Aa'\otimes b$ for $a'\in A^{p-1}$, $d(a\otimes b')=(-1)^pa\otimes d_Bb'$ for $b'\in B^{q-1}$, so changing $a$ or $b$ by a coboundary changes $a\otimes b$ by a coboundary; the class $[a\otimes b]$ is bilinear in $([a],[b])$, hence defines the map on $H^p(A)\otimes_kH^q(B)$. By Step 2, $H^n(A\otimes_kB)$ is the cohomology of the summand $H_A\otimes_kH_B$, which in degree $n$ is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H_A^p\otimes_kH_B^q$, the isomorphism being induced by the inclusion of this summand. Under the isomorphisms $H_A^p\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(A)$, $a\mapsto[a]$, and $H_B^q\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(B)$ (from $Z_A^p=B_A^p\oplus H_A^p$), this inclusion sends $[a]\otimes[b]$ to $[a\otimes b]$; so it is the map of the statement, which is therefore an isomorphism for every $n$.
